purpose: Measure the flagship 1.2B speedup over the frozen pilot recipe on rented H100 time, before grant access, so the GH200 confirmation sweep is not the first place that number is ever seen. The RTX 3090 pass selected a configuration but could only measure it on a 318M proxy; the single flagship point it produced is the eager checkpointed baseline, and no checkpointing-off flagship configuration fit the 24 GiB card at all.

funding.boundary: This packet spends no part of the 5,000-GPU-hour allocation and does not draw on the 120-hour runtime-qualification reservation. Rental cost, storage, transfer and idle time are recorded in the external rental ledger, exactly as the completed H100 pilot was.

why_h100: The H100 SXM reaches about 989.5 bf16 TFLOPS, the same peak the GH200 sweep assumes, and the pilot's 12,859 tokens/s anchor was measured on one. Deltas measured here are therefore against the same baseline hardware the numeric plan is anchored to, which the 3090 pass could not offer.
command: Each run records its exact argument vector in runs[].argv, generated and verified by experiments/qualification/check_throughput_packet.py against the real speck.training.benchmark parser. Invoke it as `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.benchmark $(argv)`; regenerate with `--print-commands` rather than hand-editing. The former prose template with {placeholder} holes is gone: it could not be checked, and its `--profile {profile}` hole took a boolean where the flag wants a trace path.

common.data_dir_note: Relative to the extracted rental bundle root, which places the packed 105M pilot pack at pilot-data/. Only the end-to-end run reads it; compute mode is synthetic. Without this the parser would silently fall back to ~/.cache/speck/benchmark-200m, which does not exist on a fresh rented host.

prerequisites: Build a fresh private bundle from a clean commit; do not reuse the historical transfer archive or its stale source pin.
Confirm the offer is an 80 GiB H100 SXM with one allocated GPU, and record instance ID, hourly rate, storage/network charges and intended deletion time.
Export a persistent TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR so max-autotune compiles once, not per run.
Record SM clock, temperature and power; reject any result whose clock moved beyond 5%.
Establish a noise band from five repeats of the first configuration before reading deltas.

runs.label: h100-pilot-baseline
runs.purpose: Reproduce the frozen pilot recipe so every later delta is a flagship delta. The pilot's own H100 rates are 12,859 tokens/s over the full trainer and 13,595 steady optimizer tokens/s; this run is the compute-mode counterpart and is not directly comparable to the full-trainer figure.

runs.label: h100-noac-eager
runs.purpose: Measure the effect of removing activation recomputation at fixed geometry; the proxy gain is not a flagship prediction.

runs.label: h100-noac-compile-mb1
runs.purpose: Measure combined model and optimizer compilation at the baseline microbatch. Record graph breaks and reasons; the proxy count is historical, not a required result.

runs.label: h100-mb2
runs.purpose: Microbatch scaling at constant global batch.

runs.label: h100-mb4
runs.purpose: Microbatch scaling; the pilot's 20% short-probe gain at microbatch four is checked here under a stable measurement.

runs.label: h100-mb8
runs.purpose: Microbatch scaling; 80 GiB should permit this where 24 GiB could not.

runs.label: h100-best-endtoend
runs.purpose: Measure packed-loader overhead against compute mode at the selected geometry. Both modes exclude startup, validation and saves; a separate sustained trainer run is required to measure the full-trainer derate.

runs.label: h100-best-profile
runs.purpose: Kernel profile on Hopper, to judge whether the KDA custom-op work is worth funding and whether FLA's Hopper-tuned autotune configurations reorder the Ampere ranking.

decisions_to_record: Flagship speedup over the baseline measured on this host at the same tokens per update. The proxy MFU establishes no flagship ceiling.
Measured estimated MFU with timing boundary and dense BF16 peak convention. Cross-device MFU alone cannot identify bandwidth or launch bottlenecks.
Loader-inclusive/compute throughput ratio, kept separate from the full-trainer derate. Leave the latter unmeasured until a sustained trainer run includes startup, validation and saves.
Measured compile gain at flagship geometry, without assuming its direction or size from the proxy.
Whether the KDA custom-op work is worth funding, judged from the Hopper profile.
does_not_transfer_to_gh200: device_batch_size. This card has 80 GiB and the GH200 has 96 GiB, so the memory-bound microbatch ceiling differs. Microbatch is immutable on resume, so it must still be frozen from the GH200 sweep and not inherited from here.
ARM64 and Grace memory/interconnect behavior, which only the grant hardware can establish.
Absolute tokens/s per allocated GPU used to re-anchor horizons. Re-anchor from the GH200 measurement; this rental narrows the uncertainty rather than closing it.
out_of_scope: Compiled execution under DistributedDataParallel. This is single-GPU, and base.py compiles the DDP-wrapped module with six graph breaks still present. Qualify it with `scripts.training_replay --compile --workers 4` on the grant hardware.
Distributed execution, scheduler requeue, long-context cost, data eligibility and model quality. None are touched here.
Any authorization to train. This is a measurement rental and admits no data.
effect_on_the_grant_sequence: A completed rental does not remove the GH200 throughput phase, which still freezes microbatch, activation checkpointing and determinism on the production hardware. It changes that phase from discovery to confirmation: the expected ranking is known in advance, a result that contradicts it is a signal to stop and diagnose rather than to explore, and the 120-hour reservation carries less risk of being spent on a surprise.
stop_conditions: Clock drift beyond 5%, unstable step times, or a graph-break count differing from the Ampere result without explanation.
Out-of-memory at a microbatch the 80 GiB card was expected to hold; record the failing configuration and stop the ladder there.
Rental spend reaching the declared ceiling; preserve every receipt and stop rather than extending.
boundary: Single-worker, single-GPU throughput measurement on rented hardware. It establishes no model quality, no data eligibility, no distributed or scheduler behavior, and no GH200 result. It consumes zero grant GPU-hours and authorizes no production training.
